title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) measuring the marginal detection benefit of sandboxed emulation over a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run accounting diagnostics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. For operational deployment, generated artifacts must be both correct and safe; the common mitigation pattern is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, often augmented by sandboxed emulation to catch runtime failures that static validators miss. Prior system and survey work argues for workflow-centred mitigations (validators, emulators, formal verifiers) but provides limited quantitative cross-vendor estimates of the marginal value added by a guarded runtime stage [1], [2].

Research question and contributions. Guided by a preregistered plan, we ask: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? We make four contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistered confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) and its faithful execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting and exact numerical reporting; (3) an interpretation rooted in validator coverage, task curation, and pipeline semantics explaining a near-zero marginal effect; and (4) reproducibility guidance and identified regimes where guarded stages are likely to add substantive value.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centric mitigation. Recent surveys and system reports document architectures that pair LLM generation with validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution to improve correctness of generated artifacts in NetOps and adjacent domains [1], [2], [3]. Those works recommend generate→validate→repair patterns but stop short of providing large-scale paired measures of guarded-stage marginal benefits.

Verifier-assisted generation and empirical evidence. Work that transfers program-verification concepts into generation tasks shows that external verifiers and simulators often catch errors that language models alone do not; empirical studies in code/specification generation and NetOps prototypes report improved correctness with external checking but heterogeneous gains depending on task and evaluator coverage [3], [4], [5]. These findings motivated our paired confirmatory design: instead of ranking models, we quantify the marginal guarded-stage detection effect under tightly controlled, preregistered conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We froze a machine-readable preregistration prior to execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics. For each pair the pipeline produced one sampled initial candidate (shared) that both the baseline and guarded conditions analyzed. Under this architecture any between-condition discordance can only arise from (i) emulation observations that reveal a violation not encoded as a validator rule or (ii) a permitted downstream repair-stage invocation recorded in run accounting. Preregistered confirmatory Npairs = 720; planned episodes = 1440 (baseline + guarded). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 (20 percentage points) used in power planning.

Task bank, vendors, and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. The bank covered three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures triggered the preregistered deterministic missingness policy (up to two automatic reseeds; irrecoverable parser failures would be excluded and replaced per the preregistration). In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model, sampling semantics, and shared_initial_candidate. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We state explicitly: temperature = null indicates the client request omitted an explicit temperature parameter; it does not imply deterministic generation (temperature=0) or provider-side determinism. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were strictly enforced: one sampled initial candidate per pair was reused by both baseline and guarded analyses and recorded in per-episode archives. Consequently, any between-condition difference is attributable only to guarded-stage emulation observations or the allowed repair-stage invocation.

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline implementation. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, command ordering/workflow, required-field presence, and policy-level constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against an emulated instance of the declared topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model call per task; run accounting shows exactly one repair-stage call in the confirmatory execution.

Execution accounting and determinism controls. The adapter family used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution manifest records model_calls_used = 721, completed_episode_count = 1440, failed_episode_count = 0. Deterministic reconciliation and provider_call_audit artifacts (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) document stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1. Contamination and provenance checks (artifact hashes and manifest records) were performed per the preregistration; no contamination flags occurred for the confirmatory set.

Scoring and primary analysis. Per-episode outcomes were binary (detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1}, detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1}) per the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor: exact McNemar two-sided test and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness handling followed complete_pair_primary (primary analysis excludes irrecoverable technical pairs); sensitivity analyses treating irrecoverable failures as nondetections were preregistered and archived but not required for the primary confirmatory estimand because there were zero technical exclusions.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (complete paired set Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) report: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All values are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and analysis artifacts.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. The execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and the deterministic_reconciliation.json provider_call_audit confirms a single repair-stage invocation. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the unique possible causes for the single n10 discordance are (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a validator violation, or (ii) the single documented repair-stage invocation. For independent verification we provide an explicit artifact pointer rather than inventing a pair identifier: the exact discordant episode is the single entry within execution/raw_results.jsonl where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that entry contains the pair_id and the validator/emulation traces linking the guarded detection to the recorded repair-stage invocation. Verification steps archived with the run: (a) open execution/raw_results.jsonl and locate the entry with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 (unique in the file); (b) read that record's pair_id and follow its validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields to confirm the repair-stage call; (c) corroborate the single-repair accounting via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json's provider_call_audit. These steps are reproducible using the archived bundle referenced by the execution manifest.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative archived examples (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, ... task-000006-*.json) include detailed validator_trace objects showing normalized_configuration, validation_before and validation_after states, validator_version = 5.0, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count. Typical traces illustrate that the vast majority of shared_initial candidates complied with validator rules (violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation observations largely duplicated validator findings. The representative artifacts thus document the validator ceiling effect evident in the aggregated counts.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy was applied deterministically; analysis/missingness_summary.csv documents complete_pairs = 720 and zero failed episodes. No deviations from the preregistration affecting the primary estimand are recorded in the archived deviation log. The contamination summary is empty for the confirmatory set (analysis/contamination_summary.csv).

Compact tabular summary (artifact-grounded). Table 1 (archived as analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) summarizes the primary confirmatory counts and statistics reported above and in analysis/results.json. These artifacts are authoritative and archived in the execution bundle.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors.

1) Validator ceiling effect. Deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic properties encoded in the synthetic task bank; baseline success rate = 0.9986111111111111. The validator's rule set covered the workflow patterns used in task generation (shutdown‑configure‑restore, make-before-break switchover, paired MTU changes), producing a ceiling that leaves little headroom for emulation to add marginal detections.

2) Task curation and inclusion policy. Confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies but not crafted adversarially to evade the validator. That curation concentrates cases inside the validator's coverage envelope and reduces the prevalence of subtle runtime-only failure modes that emulation might reveal.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. The shared-initial design isolates guarded-stage contributions but suppresses between-condition generation variability; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json record a single repair-stage invocation aligning with the single n10 discordant count. Thus the observed discordance is fully attributable to downstream guarded-stage activity recorded in run accounting rather than model-generation differences.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. The result implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs match its expected patterns (parser-validated, constrained intents), guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at aggregate scale. This conditional conclusion must not be generalized: in operational regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, stateful multi-step interactions, or validator gaps (different vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation are still likely to provide substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces support targeted follow-up hypotheses: (a) adversarial task injection will increase n10 and broaden the CI; (b) multiple validator families with complementary rule sets can reduce the ceiling effect.

Statistical sensitivity and interpretability. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) yield an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Interpreting this as a null/near-zero aggregate finding is appropriate for the specific experimental regime (synthetic parser-validated tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial semantics) but does not imply absence of practical benefit in other regimes.

Reproducibility and audit guidance. The execution bundle archives all relevant artifacts: execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and representative per-episode scoring traces under execution/scoring/. For independent verification of the discordant episode and its link to the single repair-stage call: (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl and locate the single record where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; (2) read the pair_id and inspect that record's validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields; (3) verify provider_call counts and repair_stage = 1 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. These steps are sufficient to reproduce the attribution claimed above without requiring additional runs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping via execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
